summary: Iteration 70: Full backend + frontend testing of Mira AI Studio (B2C standalone builder at /mira.ai). Note: The review request listed endpoint paths /api/studio/auth/* and /api/studio/build/* — the actual endpoints are /api/public/mira-studio/register|login, /api/mira-studio/me|buy, /api/public/mira-builder/start|status/{pid}|download/{pid}, /api/site/{slug}. All flows tested end-to-end pass, including the real AI website generation pipeline (Planner → Design → Frontend → Testing → Deployment agents) which produced a live URL serving valid HTML within 60s. Razorpay order creation + checkout iframe load also verified. Salon SaaS regression passed.
action_items: None — feature working as designed. Note for main agent: the endpoint paths in the review request (/api/studio/auth/register, /api/studio/build/website, etc.) are aspirational — the actual mounted routes are /api/public/mira-studio/* and /api/public/mira-builder/*. If the intent was to rename them, main agent should update either code or the spec.
critical_code_review_comments: mira_builder.py is 457 lines — still manageable but approaching the 700-line split threshold; keep an eye on it.

Route paths in this router (/public/mira-studio, /mira-studio, /public/mira-builder, /site) are inconsistent — some are 'studio' scoped, others 'builder' scoped. Consider unifying under /studio/* for clarity as the product matures.

_studio_user uses generic jwt_secret / make_access shared with salon SaaS — tokens issued to studio users would decode as salon users too since the /api/auth endpoints use the same secret. This is fine today because studio_users collection is separate and lookups are scoped, but flag: a salon-admin JWT and a studio-user JWT with the same subject id would each be valid on the other's endpoints. Consider a separate audience/claim ('aud':'studio') and verifying it in _studio_user.
public_rate_limit for /public/mira-studio/register is 6/hour per IP — legitimate for prod but tight for testing; consider whitelisting in preview or bumping when running heavy regression suites.
Website build pipeline OK; refund path (_fail_and_refund) exists. Suggest logging refund amounts in a ledger collection for audit.

seed_data_creation: Each test class creates its own studio_user via /api/public/mira-studio/register. One website project built end-to-end (Aura salon), one insufficient-credits scenario (broke user, 2x app builds).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Studio user tokens go in localStorage as 'mira_studio_token'. The credits badge click can be intercepted by the success toast in the top-right — wait ~3s after registration before clicking it (or use JS .click()). Razorpay iframe loads to api.razorpay.com/v1/checkout/public — payments should NEVER be completed in preview. Backend AI builds take 30-60s per website, 60-90s per app; use 180s timeout when polling status.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. Two initial test-script problems (email uppercase mismatch, buy modal opening blocked by toast overlay) were test-side and were resolved by using lowercased emails and pre-authenticating via API + localStorage token injection.
